title: Queue-row predicate diverges between noc_queue_rows and the draw loop at amber_pct==0 (pre-existing, carried over by the re-key)
detail: At amber_pct==0 the count proc counts only queued ports (amber_pct>0 guard) but the draw skip condition never skips (util_pct < 0 is false), so every port row draws — section row budget undercounts. Pre-existing divergence both hunks preserve unchanged.
recommended_fix: Align the predicates: in the draw loop skip when q-sum==0 && (amber_pct == 0 || util_pct < u32(amber_pct)), or drop the amber_pct>0 guard from noc_queue_rows.

title: Bare-form NOC queue id fallback is never measured — the never-overlap guarantee is asserted only by comment
detail: Only the full R-form is measured (fw); the bare "%d>%d" fallback is assumed ≤68px by comment. Router/peer ids of 4+ digits would exceed the 68px gutter and run under the lane letters anyway.
recommended_fix: Measure the bare form too (or truncate/clamp the label to NOC_Q_LABEL_MAX) so the never-overlap guarantee holds for any id width.

title: Drive-by punctuation edit in an assertion message unrelated to the file's S5 change
evidence:
-	testing.expect(t, f_after == table3[5], "the tick after A resolves: the basis switches to B's own onset — phase 5, the DIP")
+	testing.expect(t, f_after == table3[5], "the tick after A resolves: the basis switches to B's own onset - phase 5, the DIP")
detail: Unexplained em-dash → hyphen edit in a test message string, functionally inert and unrelated to the file's crisis_trigger signature change; looks like unaccounted-for churn in the diff.
recommended_fix: Revert the punctuation change, or record the reason (e.g. source-encoding normalization) in the commit message.
